items.title: Bennie Turner Interview, 1972-02-09
items.q: when I joined his band... The only thing we had that was very good was what Pete wanted on piano. What Pete and Charlie Bocas wanted out of a piano.

ctx.x: Most of that I was over the age. I was 32, you see, when I was in the Southern. Oh, I see. The only thing we had that was very good was what Pete wanted on piano.
What Pete and Charlie Bocas wanted out of a piano.

Yeah. Well it was hard on piano players and drummers, you see, and all. My, I was used to playing mostly stock numbers, you know, orchestrations, and giving the band support, compliments more, you know. And when I joined his band, well he wanted to lead, fill in them, you see. Yeah. He didn't believe in your countenance. Playing chords. No, he didn't believe in playing chords. And the drummers, he was hard on them with the tempos, you know, trying to hold his tempo that he set. He would complain if they speeded…
